items.bewering: Die Egiptenare het geglo dat 'n farao ná sy dood verder leef.
items.bron: Metropolitan Museum, essay 'Egypt in the Old Kingdom (ca. 2649-2150 B.C.)' (metmuseum.org/essays) - the king's afterlife was central, and officials' afterlife may have depended on the king's; the Pyramid Texts carved inside Unas's pyramid form a ritual guiding the king to life after death (thecollector.com, 'What the Pyramid Texts Reveal About the Egyptian Afterlife').

items.bewering: Daarom het hulle vir baie farao's 'n reusagtige graf van groot klipblokke gebou.
items.bron: Wikipedia, 'Egyptian pyramids' - between 118 and 138 pyramids identified in Egypt, most of them tombs for pharaohs and their consorts in the Old and Middle Kingdoms. 'Baie' is correct and not overstated: not all pharaohs got one (New Kingdom kings were buried in rock-cut tombs in the Valley of the Kings - National Geographic, 'Valley of the Kings'), and Middle Kingdom pyramids were mainly mudbrick, but the sentence says 'baie', not 'alle'.

items.bewering: So 'n graf word 'n piramide genoem
items.bron: Metropolitan Museum, 'Egypt in the Old Kingdom' essay - at Giza 'many officials were buried within two vast cemeteries of stone mastabas'; Wikipedia, 'Mastaba' - a mastaba is a flat-roofed, rectangular tomb with sloping sides, monumental ones often of limestone, and at least 150 were built beside the Giza pyramids. A huge tomb of large stone blocks is therefore not necessarily a pyramid. The lesson never says anywhere what a pyramid looks like, so the only thing it names as making a tomb 'a pyramid' (size and stone blocks) also fits a mastaba, which is not one. What makes a pyramid a pyramid is its shape.
items.regstelling: The sentence that names the pyramid must carry its shape, which is the distinguishing feature: a pyramid is such a tomb with a square base and four sloping sides that meet in a point at the top. As it stands, 'a huge tomb of large stone blocks is called a pyramid' is too wide, because a large stone mastaba fits it too.

items.bewering: party ander belangrike mense het ook een gekry.
items.bron: Wikipedia, 'Pyramid G1-b' and 'Pyramid G1-c'; ancientegyptonline.co.uk, 'Great Pyramid Complex: The Queen's Pyramids' - three small pyramids beside Khufu's Great Pyramid were built for queens or royal women (attributions to individual queens are debated, but that they were for royal women is not). Wikipedia, 'Egyptian pyramids': most were tombs for pharaohs and their consorts.

items.bewering: Die bou van so 'n reusagtige graf het baie beplanning gevra. Die bouers moes elke kant en elke hoek noukeurig meet.
items.bron: Wikipedia, 'Great Pyramid of Giza' - the base sides differ in length by only about 58 mm on average, the corners are square to a mean error of 12 arc seconds, and the sides are aligned to the compass directions to within about a tenth of a degree. That precision requires careful measurement of every side and corner.

items.bewering: Duisende werkers het jare lank saam aan 'n groot piramide gewerk.
items.bron: Wikipedia, 'Great Pyramid of Giza' - construction about 26 years (classical sources say 20); a construction-management study estimated an average of about 13 200 workers and a peak around 40 000. AERA-associated estimates range from about 10 000 (Redding, from food remains) to 20 000-30 000 (Lehner, from the workers' town). Every estimate is in the thousands and every duration is in years, so 'duisende' and 'jare lank' hold.

items.bewering: By Giza staan drie bekende piramides naby mekaar.
items.bron: Britannica, 'Pyramids of Giza' (search summary); Afrikaans Wikipedia, 'Piramides van Giza' - the three main pyramids, of Khufu, Khafre and Menkaure, stand together on the Giza plateau and were built over three generations.

items.bewering: Die Groot Piramide is al meer as 4 500 jaar oud.
items.bron: Wikipedia, 'Great Pyramid of Giza' - built around 2600 BC for Khufu; reanalysis of radiocarbon samples puts completion between 2620 and 2484 BC. Britannica's Khufu dates (c. 2575-2465 BC for the period) and its 4th-dynasty dates also place it before 2474 BC. Even the youngest end of any range (2484 BC) makes it about 4 510 years old in 2026, so 'meer as 4 500 jaar' holds on every chronology found.

items.bewering: Die Groot Piramide (the name implies it is the largest of the three)
items.bron: Wikipedia, 'Great Pyramid of Giza' - it is the largest of the Egyptian pyramids (originally 146.6 m high, now 138.5 m). The lesson makes no explicit superlative claim; this item records that the size implied by the name is correct. No other superlative ('eerste', 'oudste', 'grootste', 'enigste') appears anywhere in the lesson.

items.bewering: Die ander twee is dié van Chafra (in Engels: Khafre) en Menkaoere (in Engels: Menkaure).
items.bron: Harvard Giza Project, 'Khafre Pyramid' (giza.digitalhumanities.fas.harvard.edu); brewminate.com, 'The Pyramids of Khufu, Khafre, Menkaure and the Great Sphinx at Giza' - the second and third pyramids are Khafre's and Menkaure's. Afrikaans Wikipedia, 'Piramides van Giza', uses exactly 'Piramide van Chafra' and 'Piramide van Menkaoere', so the Afrikaans spellings are attested; Khafre and Menkaure are the standard English forms.

items.bewering: Die Groot Sfinks is 'n reusagtige beeld met 'n leeu se liggaam en 'n mens se kop.
items.bron: Britannica, 'Great Sphinx of Giza' (search summary) - a colossal limestone statue with a lion's body and a human head wearing a royal headdress; Wikipedia, 'Great Sphinx of Giza' - about 73 m long and 20 m high.

items.bewering: Bouers het dit naby die piramides uit die kalksteen van die plek self gekap.
items.bron: Wikipedia, 'Great Sphinx of Giza' - a monolith 'carved from the bedrock of the plateau', on the Giza plateau beside the pyramids; Britannica: carved from a single piece of limestone. (Later restorations added limestone blocks, which does not affect the claim that it was carved from the site's own rock.)

items.bewering: Dit was moontlik 'n beskermer van die piramides.
items.bron: Wikipedia, 'Great Sphinx of Giza' - no contemporary text states its purpose; the guardian reading is one established interpretation (medieval Arab writers already called it a talisman guarding the area), alongside a link to the sun god Hor-em-akhet. Mainstream accounts summarise it as a guardian of the Giza necropolis while noting the purpose is debated (historyskills.com, 'The Great Sphinx: exploring the enigma of its creation and purpose'). The lesson's 'moontlik' matches the state of knowledge exactly; the hedge must stay if the sentence is touched.

items.bewering: Tempels was geboue waar die Egiptenare hulle gode vereer het.
items.bron: Egypt Exploration Society, 'Temples in Ancient Egypt' (ees.ac.uk); Wikipedia, 'Egyptian temple' - temples were the houses of the gods where they were served and honoured. Note for a person, not a fault: most ceremonies were closed to ordinary people, who could not enter the inner temple, but people of all classes came to temples to pray and make offerings in the outer parts, so the general statement is true.

items.bewering: Hulle het geglo dat 'n god self in sy tempel woon.
items.bron: Egypt Exploration Society, 'Temples in Ancient Egypt' - 'Gods were believed to live within their statues in the temple's shrine'; Wikipedia, 'Egyptian temple' - the god's ba was believed to inhabit the cult statue in the sanctuary.

items.bewering: Kop 'Huise vir die gode' - the temple compared to a house in which the god lives.
items.bron: Wikipedia, 'Egyptian temple' - the Egyptian word for temple, hwt-ntr, means 'mansion (or enclosure) of a god'; EES: 'A temple was a house for the one or more deities it was dedicated to.' The mapping holds where a learner would take it: the god was believed to live there, was woken, washed, dressed and fed daily like a household's occupant, and ordinary people did not walk in freely. It is the Egyptians' own image, not an imported one.

items.bewering: Priesters het elke dag daar rituele vir die god uitgevoer.
items.bron: Egypt Exploration Society, 'Temples in Ancient Egypt' - the 'daily ritual' in which the statue was woken, fed and dressed, performed each morning by the high priest acting for the pharaoh; Wikipedia, 'Egyptian temple' - daily offering rituals at sunrise by the officiating priest; temple rituals were a duty of priests.

items.bewering: Die piramides, die Sfinks en baie tempels staan vandag nog.
items.blok: Ons kan dit vandag nog sien
items.bron: Wikipedia, 'Great Pyramid of Giza' - the only one of the Seven Wonders largely intact; Wikipedia, 'Egyptian temple' - 'dozens of sites with substantial temple remains', with Karnak, Luxor and Abu Simbel well preserved; UNESCO lists Memphis and its Necropolis (Giza to Dahshur) as a World Heritage site.

items.bewering: Mense van regoor die wêreld kom kyk na hierdie erfenis.
items.blok: Ons kan dit vandag nog sien
items.bron: Wikipedia, 'Egyptian temple' - well-preserved temples 'draw tourists from around the world' and are a key attraction of Egypt's tourist industry; UNESCO state-of-conservation reports for Memphis and its Necropolis (whc.unesco.org/en/soc/4234) list the growing number of visitors as a factor affecting the site.

items.bewering: Die klipgeboue is ook bewyse van hoe goed die Egiptenare kon beplan en bou.
items.blok: Ons kan dit vandag nog sien
items.bron: Interpretive, and supported: Wikipedia, 'Great Pyramid of Giza' - base sides within about 58 mm of each other and corners square to 12 arc seconds; it was the tallest human-made structure for more than 3 700 years.

items.bewering: piramide: In antieke Egipte: 'n groot graf, gewoonlik van klipblokke, wat vir 'n farao of ander belangrike mens gebou is.
items.bron: Read alone, as a definition this entry also fits a mastaba, which is not a pyramid: Metropolitan Museum, 'Egypt in the Old Kingdom' - Giza officials were buried in 'two vast cemeteries of stone mastabas'; Wikipedia, 'Mastaba' - flat-roofed rectangular tombs, the monumental ones often of limestone, built for high officials and royalty, at least 150 of them beside the Giza pyramids. A large stone tomb for an important person is exactly what this entry describes. Every pyramid fits the entry, but not everything that fits the entry is a pyramid; the entry leaves out the one thing the word names, the shape.
items.regstelling: The entry must include the shape: in ancient Egypt, a large tomb with a square base and four sloping sides that meet in a point at the top, usually built of stone blocks for a pharaoh or another important person. The rest of the entry ('gewoonlik van klipblokke', 'farao of ander belangrike mens') is correct and can stay.

items.bewering: sfinks: 'n Beeld van 'n wese met 'n leeu se liggaam en gewoonlik 'n mens se kop.
items.bron: New World Encyclopedia, 'Sphinx'; Wikipedia, 'Sphinx' - Egyptian sphinxes have a lion's body with a human head (androsphinx), a ram's head (criosphinx, e.g. the avenue at Karnak) or a falcon's head (hieracosphinx); the human head is the most common. 'Gewoonlik' is therefore exactly right. The Greek mythical sphinx (lion's body, woman's head, wings) also fits the entry, so it holds read alone.

items.bewering: tempel: 'n Gebou waar mense 'n god of gode vereer.
items.bron: Egypt Exploration Society, 'Temples in Ancient Egypt'; Wikipedia, 'Egyptian temple' - a building dedicated to one or more deities, where they were served and honoured. The general sense of the word.

items.bewering: kalksteen: 'n Soort rots wat mense uitkap om mee te bou en waarin water grotte kan uitvreet.
items.bron: US National Park Service, 'Solution Caves' (nps.gov/subjects/caves/solution-caves.htm) - solution caves form when acidic water dissolves rock and are most often found in limestone; USGS, 'Geology of Mammoth Cave National Park' - the cave was dissolved in limestone; USGS fact sheet via geology.com - limestone is widely quarried as building stone (and the Giza monuments themselves are of quarried limestone).

items.bewering: vereer: Om aan 'n god of 'n persoon groot eer en respek te bewys.
items.bron: WordReference Dutch-English (jann.wordreference.com, 'veneration'/'revere') gives Dutch 'vereren' as to revere or honour with deep respect; Afrikaans usage in NGTT (ojs.reformedjournals.co.za) uses 'vereer' for honouring someone as king. No online WAT/HAT entry could be retrieved; the sense given matches the cognate and the attested Afrikaans use, and it does not claim worship in the strict sense ('aanbid'), which is correct.

items.bewering: priester: In antieke Egipte: iemand wat in 'n tempel gewerk en daar rituele vir die gode uitgevoer het.
items.bron: Wikipedia, 'Egyptian temple' - the pharaoh delegated temple rites to priests, and performing them was a priestly duty; EES, 'Temples in Ancient Egypt' - priests performed the daily ritual for the god.

items.bewering: ritueel: 'n Vaste reeks handelinge wat mense elke keer op dieselfde manier doen, dikwels vir 'n god.
items.bron: Wikipedia, 'Ritual' - a sequence of activities performed according to a set order; dictionary sense quoted in search results: 'a religious or solemn ceremony involving a series of actions performed according to a set order' and 'a set of fixed actions ... performed regularly'. 'Dikwels vir 'n god' correctly allows for secular rituals.

items.bewering: erfenis: Dinge en gewoontes wat ons uit die verlede ontvang, bewaar en aan die volgende geslagte oordra.
items.bron: Wiktionary, Dutch 'erfenis' - besides the legal sense (an estate inherited from a deceased person) it means heritage (erfgoed); National Heritage Resources Act 25 of 1999 and SAHRA regulations (acts.co.za) - heritage resources are places and objects of cultural significance conserved 'for future generations'. The entry gives the heritage sense, which is the one the lesson uses; it does not cover the legal inheritance sense, which is an omission of a second meaning, not a falsehood.

opsomming: One fault, in two places: the lesson calls a huge tomb of stone blocks a pyramid without ever saying what a pyramid looks like, so both the opening block and the glossary entry also fit the flat-topped stone tombs (mastabas) that officials were buried in right beside the Giza pyramids; the shape (square base, four sloping sides meeting in a point) must be added, and everything else, including the 4 500-year age, the Chafra and Menkaoere spellings and the hedged 'moontlik' guardian claim for the Sphinx, checks out.
